subject: ClearVault pilot: Private deploy qualification — data handling & egress constraints
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita@clearvault.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: ClearVault pilot: Private deploy qualification — data handling & egress constraints

Hi Anita — thanks again for taking time today. Quick written recap from our discovery so we have the questions captured and can align on a pilot scope. TL;DR: ClearVault is interested in a Private (VPC/on-prem) pilot to meet data residency & logging controls for PII workloads.

Call highlights:
- Use case: customer support & KYC validation; smallish traffic for pilot (~2k requests/day).
- Required assurances: PII redaction controls, configurable retention, and strict egress limits (no unmediated internet egress).
- Preference to host in ClearVault's VPC with a customer-controlled gateway (proxy) or in an air-gapped pilot if needed for certain environments.

Open items we need from you (can reply inline):
1) Sensitive data categories — please confirm which fields are considered PII for the pilot (names, SSNs, emails, payment tokens, call transcripts?).
2) Retention policy target — what is the required retention for request/response logs and audit trails (days/months)?
3) Logging and evidence — which logs do you need for audit (request metadata, full request/response, model prompts, infrastructure-level logs)? Any required format (CSV, JSON) or retention policy for audit exports?
4) Network egress: do you allow outbound TLS only to a small set of CIDRs/IPs, or must the deployment be fully offline (air-gap)? If proxy, please supply IP ranges and proxy host details or a contact who owns the network whitelist.
5) Compliance artifacts: SOC2/ISO attachments you can share to speed evidence collection.

Attachments: initial-network-sketch.svg (rough sketch from the call).

Proposed next steps and owners:
- You: send PII list + retention target and proxy/IPs (Anita) — target: 6/15
- Redwood Security: map required evidence and confirm what we can provide in a Private deployment (Lauren) — target: 6/14
- Redwood Eng: prepare a minimal config for air-gapped pilot and list of required customer-side firewall openings (Marcus & Evelyn) — target: 6/18

If anything above is off, correct me. Otherwise propose a 30-min technical follow-up on Wednesday 6/16 to lock the whitelist and retention windows.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[attachment: initial-network-sketch.svg (image/svg+xml)]

From: Anita Rao <anita@clearvault.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@clearvault.com, procurement@clearvault.com
Date: 2027-06-13T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClearVault pilot: Private deploy qualification — data handling & egress constraints

Thanks Marcus — good summary. Quick answers inline below and a couple of clarifications. Forwarding to our security and procurement leads to keep everyone aligned.

1) PII scope: primary for pilot will be customer full name, email, transaction IDs, and limited financial identifiers (last 4 digits only). We do not want full SSNs in logs. We will attach our classification table for reference.

2) Retention: for the pilot, security requires 90 days for request metadata and 30 days for full request/response payloads. Audit logs (authn/authz events) should be retained for 365 days.

3) Logs & evidence: security wants immutable audit trails for admin actions, request/response hashes (we can accept hashed prompts), and access logs with user principal. Export format: JSON preferred, daily roll-up optional. We will upload a short evidence checklist to your Drive link.

4) Network: we do not run fully offline. Preferred approach is VPC-hosted with egress only to a managed proxy that inspects outbound traffic. We can provide a small set of static egress IPs (will share by EOD). No direct outbound to public cloud storage endpoints unless explicitly whitelisted.

5) Compliance artifacts: attached is our classification workbook. We can share a SOC2 snapshot once an NDA appendix is in place.

Attachments: sensitive-data-classification.xlsx

Can Lauren confirm whether Redwood can support differential retention windows (30/90/365) per log type, and whether token-level logs can be disabled for a private deployment? Also, do you have a simple diagram showing where the audit log exports land (we'd like to see the pipeline to our SIEM).

Best,
Anita Rao
Security & Privacy Lead
ClearVault
[attachment: sensitive-data-classification.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita@clearvault.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-13T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClearVault pilot: Private deploy qualification — data handling & egress constraints

Hi Anita — looping in the technical answers below and a short summary of what we can commit for the pilot. Apologies for the detailed note but wanted to be explicit.

Retention and logs:
- We support per-log-type retention windows in Private deployments. For the pilot we can configure: request/response payloads (30 days), request metadata (90 days), and immutable admin/audit logs (365 days) as you requested.
- Token-level logs: by default Redwood does not persist raw model token streams in Private deployments unless the customer configures "detailed-token-logging." We can disable token persistence entirely for your pilot; operational traces (latency metrics, token counts) will still be available for SLO monitoring but are aggregated and not queryable as raw tokens.
- Export format: JSON daily rollups are supported and we can deliver an automated S3/HTTP push to your SIEM endpoint. For air-gapped customers we provide an export bundle you can pull from an internal location.

Audit and evidence:
- Immutable audit trail: available; stores admin actions, role changes, and API keys issuance events. We can provide a signed daily digest for the pilot if needed.
- SOC2 snapshot: we can provide a redacted SOC2 report under NDA; procurement/security can take next steps to request an appendix.

Network & egress model:
- Options supported:
  1) VPC-hosted + customer-managed proxy (preferred): Redwood services run in your subnet, and outbound to Redwood-managed model runtime is limited through your proxy. You provide static egress IPs and proxy host(s).
  2) Air-gapped: we ship an offline runtime bundle and management plane connectors; this requires an initial secure transfer and an on-site engineer for setup. No outbound internet traffic required.
  3) Hybrid (pull model): runtime in VPC with strict egress to a small set of Redwood endpoints (we provide CIDRs) — useful when you allow a managed link to our runtime.
- For the pilot we recommend (1) if you can provide proxy/egress IPs; (2) if your compliance team cannot permit any outbound, we can scope an air-gapped pilot but expect longer setup time (2–3 weeks).

Attachments: private-deploy-config.pdf (sample config and what we need from your firewall team).

Questions for ClearVault:
- Can you confirm the SIEM ingest method (S3 push vs HTTP) and a test endpoint?
- Please share the static egress IPs and the contact for your network/security engineer.

I'll draft a short pilot runbook after we confirm those two items.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
[attachment: private-deploy-config.pdf (application/pdf)]
